owner_request.request: Projected growth for each fund over 3 years, the horizon of the house goal, so the Guild can show what each fund could be worth and which exposures grow most.

what_is_projected: the fund's annualized total return over the next 36 months, as a range (10th, 50th, 90th percentile) and the chance of ending below where it started
applies_to: model-universe funds in a peer group with a reference fund; no projection for INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, SPECIALIZED_LEVERAGED, SPECIALIZED_INVERSE or IDIOSYNCRATIC (leveraged and inverse funds decay with the path, and ungrouped funds have no long reference history)
reference: the fund's nearest reference fund from its point-in-time peer classification; US large growth and value funds use VUG and VTV
cash: BIL total return and trailing 12-month distribution yield; SHY before BIL has 12 months of history

center_candidates.CASH_PLUS_BETA: today's cash yield + the fund's beta to its reference x the reference's annualized excess return over cash across all of its history up to the month-end - (fund fee - reference fee)
center_candidates.REFERENCE_HISTORY: the reference's annualized total return across all of its history up to the month-end - (fund fee - reference fee)
center_candidates.OWN_HISTORY: the fund's own annualized total return over its last 120 months (at least 60 required)
center_candidates.BOND_YIELD: bond families only: the fund's trailing 12-month distribution yield

center_selection: walk-forward by family: for each test start, the candidate with the lowest median absolute error (projected center against realized 36-month annualized return) over earlier starts whose 36 months had fully ended; with fewer than 3 such earlier starts the default is used
fee_source: official SEC expense ratio on or before the month-end; zero gap when either fee is missing
spread: the reference's monthly log returns across all of its history up to the month-end, de-meaned, scaled by the ratio of the fund's to the reference's monthly volatility over the trailing 36 months, and resampled in 12-month blocks into 36-month paths (2,000 paths, fixed seed); the percentiles are the center plus the resampled spread

test.starts: every December month-end from 2005 to the last one whose 36 months have ended
test.observations: every model-universe fund with a projection at that start and a realized 36-month return
measures: share of realized returns inside the 10th-90th percentile band (overall, by family, by start year)
share below the 10th and above the 90th percentile
median absolute error of the center, chosen rule against OWN_HISTORY
test.clustering_note: funds starting in the same year share one market path, so coverage is also reported by start year; a pass means the bands were honest on average, not in every year

if_passes: the Guild shows each fund's 3-year range labelled tested, with the measured coverage
if_fails: the Guild still shows the ranges but labels them not calibrated, with the measured coverage, and makes no growth ranking from them
what_it_is_not: not a pick of next year's winners within a peer group (the ranking trials found no price signal that does that); the projection's differences between funds come from exposure, beta, volatility and fee
known_limitations: Survivorship: the model universe is funds alive today, so the test omits funds that closed.
Reference histories start between 1993 and 2018; the longest is SPY's.
Distribution yield is a stand-in for a bond fund's yield to maturity, which the free data does not carry.

amendments.change: Each family is judged on its own band instead of one family failing the whole test. A family whose 10th-90th band held between 60% and 95% of outcomes (with at least 200 observations) is TESTED; above 95% it is TOO_CAUTIOUS; below 60% it is TOO_NARROW. Ranges always show with their family's status and measured coverage; growth is compared only among funds in TESTED families.
amendments.reason: The registered test failed only because international equity bands were too wide (95.6% of outcomes inside against a 95% ceiling), the cautious direction; overall coverage was 82.7% inside the 70-90% mark. Recorded as a change made after seeing results.

amendments.change: No projection for a fund whose beta to its reference or to the S&P 500 exceeds 2.0, or whose volatility exceeds 2.5 times its reference's, over the trailing 36 months (reason MOVES_FAR_MORE_THAN_ITS_REFERENCE). The test was re-run with this guard.
amendments.reason: Reviewing the live package showed leveraged funds the returns-based classifier had not flagged (for example 3x sector funds in US large cap, with typical projections above 40% a year) and poorly matched funds (international bonds placed with short Treasuries at beta 4.9). The registered scope already excluded leveraged funds; the guard enforces that intent by behaviour rather than by name. A 2x Nasdaq fund measured only 1.5 against the technology reference, so the S&P 500 beta is checked too.

amendments.change: display_rule: the owner asked to sort and filter single funds by the typical 3-year figure on the Market Board. Allowed, with the caveat shown whenever that sort is on: within a peer group a higher figure mostly means a fund that swings more than its peers, which did not pay more in the trials, and own-history figures are weaker still. Ranking calls are unchanged (cost within peer group).

display_rule: Growth is compared between peer groups (what a fund holds), never as a ranking of single funds: within a group a higher projection mostly reflects higher beta, and the ranking trials found volatility and beta did not pick winners within a group.
